value.body: A freight forwarding executive organises how a client's goods move between countries — choosing sea or air routes, booking space, preparing documents and tracking cargo. Employers include freight forwarders, logistics companies and the shipping teams of exporters. The role may be on the operations side (bookings and tracking) or the sales side (finding clients and quoting rates).

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com International Business, BBA or any graduate; logistics certificate courses help

items.label: Key terms
items.value: Incoterms, bill of lading, air waybill, FCL/LCL

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Forwarding software, carrier booking portals, Excel, email

items.label: Cargo handled at major ports
items.note: ~1,597 million tonnes across all Indian ports
items.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways data (as reported)

items.label: Container cargo at major ports
items.note: Sea freight is only part of forwarding work; air cargo is separate
items.source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways data (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join forwarders in port and airport cities as operations or documentation trainees, or in sales-support roles. Knowledge of Incoterms and shipping documents from the degree or a short course helps.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work follows global shipping schedules; late or early calls are common.
Next roles: senior executive, pricing specialist, branch or key account manager.
Freight rates swing with global events, which affects workload and targets.

competition.note: B.Com graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Com graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
